name: aes-maturity
description: Assess project maturity with a versioned rubric and immutable evidence snapshots, separating implementation, verified mechanisms, and user outcomes. Does not manage roadmap state or authorize releases.
---

# Evidence-calibrated maturity

Use the [generic rubric](references/rubric.json) by default. The [fund research profile](references/fund-research.md) is optional and is not a private project assessment.

Pin repository revision, scope ID, rubric version and observation time. Read the previous snapshot only when scope and rubric match. For every dimension record score or unknown, evidence owner/path/revision, stage, confidence, negative evidence, and limits. Missing evidence stays unknown; it does not silently become zero or success.

Evidence strength: observed user outcome with independent review; real integration seam; provider-free selected tests; source inspection; accepted specification; draft or marketing description. Each proves only its own scope. File delivery is not useful advice, and a model response is not correctness.

Keep mechanical maturity separate from actual user value. Compare only like scope/rubric. Classify movement as product change, new evidence, reclassification, error correction or unchanged. Same evidence retains its score; changed unverified seams become changed_unknown, not automatic regression or improvement. Preserve earlier records and correct with a new linked record.

The default rubric and optional 24-goal, 28-capability and 16-strategic profiles are generic adaptations with new scale identities, not private historical assessments or comparable historical scales. Offline calculators retain evidence checks and arithmetic mechanisms; read [calculator guide](references/calculators.md) before selecting a profile. Do not import old private scores or claim comparability. Report dimension scores separately; do not turn an average into task success rate.

Write a proposed local snapshot at the user's chosen path. Report progress, demonstrated stage, top remaining gaps and actions, then the scoring table. Do not publish automatically, initiate paid models, modify a roadmap, close a spec or treat a score as release approval. Link optional roadmap work only when it is separately requested.
